thesis: Luka Dončić faced significant durability challenges in the 2024-25 season, suffering multiple injuries—including calf, groin, finger and hamstring strains—that limited him to a career-low appearance rate, culminating in a Grade 2 hamstring strain in April.

facts.claim: Dončić appeared in 50 games during 2024-25, his lowest total of his NBA career.
He missed time with a calf contusion, left finger sprain, and left groin soreness during the 2024-25 season.
Dončić suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain on April 2, 2026, against Oklahoma City that forced him out for the remainder of the regular season.
During his first six NBA seasons, Dončić suited up in at least 65 games five times before dropping to 50 in 2024-25.
Despite injury issues, Dončić averaged 33.4 points, 7.9 rebounds and 8.7 assists per game heading into late January 2026.
According to injury expert Jeff Stotts, Grade 2 hamstring strains average 35 days of time lost.
